summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p allogeneic cord transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea lasting five days. He was found to be dehydrated with orthostatic hypotension and acute kidney injury, with creatinine rising from a baseline of 1.8 to 3.0. IV hydration was initiated, and his renal function improved, returning to baseline by discharge. Stool testing was positive for norovirus, and flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsy showed no evidence of graft-versus-host disease. Liver enzymes remained elevated throughout admission, prompting consultation with the liver team and plans for close outpatient monitoring; allopurinol was discontinued, and Bactrim was held due to transaminitis. The patient's gastrointestinal symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up on liver function and restart medications as appropriate.
